daily.brief: 過去約30小時（16日凌晨3:30到17日上午9:17）有594則帖、166個帳號。最乾淨的多頭是$SPCX，10個帳號一致看好、零看淡，Nvidia 13F加碼持股被多次點名。MSFT因全球中斷被5個帳號看淡，SMH也有5個帳號因芯片弱勢轉空。NVDA依舊是最大熱點，199則帖裡看淡帳號明顯多（25對14）。
daily.full:
共識

SPCX這輪最明確，10個帳號看好、沒有看淡，28則帖。@Hedgeye詳述Nvidia 13F將SpaceX持股增加6%至1.305億股，同時減持Intel。原帖。@wallstengine也提到Nvidia Q3增購約770萬股，持股價值197億美元。原帖。@rubicon59則對Druckenmiller新加入SPCX倉位表示「我批准」。原帖。

XLP、LLY、CGON、UBER、CVX、WMT各有2個帳號站多頭。@philrosenn仍認為Eli Lilly複利穩定，可能成為標普最大股票，肥胖藥物還早。原帖。@Couzin_Vinny則提醒LLY股價被釘在1440看漲牆附近，建議等遠離或gamma到期後再加。原帖。

共同看淡

MSFT有5個帳號明確看淡，10則帖。@DeItaone指出微軟揭示導致全球中斷的數月老漏洞，自7月未偵測，影響Outlook、Teams等。原帖。@HedgeyeTech把MSFT中斷、FAA、UAL、銀行中斷串在一起，說有事發生。原帖。

SMH同樣5個看淡。@EliteOptions2提到芯片與記憶體股領跌，MU跌7.4%、SNDK跌8.2%。原帖。@OptionsMike說SMH仍是弱點。UAL因廣泛系統中斷阻止航班起飛也被多個帳號點名看淡，@KobeissiLetter和@TrendSpider都發了突發。原帖 原帖。

分歧

NVDA是絕對主角，199則帖，看好14個帳號、看淡25個。@wallstengine提到Vera Rubin首批MLPerf結果，在全部7項AI訓練基準領先，每GPU速度較GB300最高快2倍。原帖。@Mr_Derivatives則表示全力做多。但看淡聲音仍明顯較多。@WheelieInvestor甚至拋出因GTA6而GPU與RAM再漲10倍的可能性，目標價SNDK 10000、MU 2000、NVDA 500，說無人預期此事。原帖。

QQQ有5對9，33則帖；SPY有2對8，38則帖。指數偏空，但個股如SPCX和部分消費股仍有支持。

其他值得留意

整體來看，太空名字因13F加碼獲共識，科技中斷和芯片弱勢則帶來看淡，大票NVDA持續分裂。594則帖來自166個帳號，討論集中在這幾個主題。

SPCX獲10個帳號共識看好，Nvidia 13F加碼持股至1.305億股被多次提及。NVDA有199則帖，看淡帳號明顯多過看好（25對14），雖有Vera Rubin基準正面結果。MSFT因全球中斷被5個帳號看淡，SMH也因芯片弱勢有壓力。

daily.brief: Over the past ~30 hours (early morning of the 16th at 03:30 to morning of the 17th at 09:17) there were 594 posts from 166 accounts. The cleanest long is $SPCX, with 10 accounts bullish and zero bearish, as Nvidia’s 13F stake increase was repeatedly noted. MSFT was bearish from 5 accounts due to global outages, and SMH also had 5 accounts turning negative on chip weakness. NVDA remains the biggest hotspot, with 199 posts where bearish accounts clearly outnumber bullish ones (25 vs 14).
daily.full:
Consensus

SPCX was the clearest this round, 10 bullish accounts and no bearish, 28 posts. @Hedgeye detailed Nvidia’s 13F increasing SpaceX holdings by 6% to 130.5 million shares while reducing Intel. original post. @wallstengine also noted Nvidia bought about 7.7 million shares in Q3, valuing the stake at $19.7 billion. original post. @rubicon59 said “I approve” of Druckenmiller’s new SPCX position. original post.

XLP, LLY, CGON, UBER, CVX, WMT each have 2 accounts on the long side. @philrosenn still sees Eli Lilly’s compounding as steady, potentially becoming the largest S&P stock, with obesity drugs still early. original post. @Couzin_Vinny notes LLY is pinned near the 1440 call wall and suggests waiting until it moves away or after gamma expiry to add. original post.

Joint Bearish

MSFT has 5 accounts clearly bearish, 10 posts. @DeItaone pointed out Microsoft revealed a months-old bug causing the global outage, undetected since July, affecting Outlook, Teams, etc. original post. @HedgeyeTech linked the MSFT outage with FAA, UAL, and bank disruptions, saying something is going on. original post.

SMH also has 5 bearish. @EliteOptions2 noted chips and memory stocks led the decline, with MU down 7.4% and SNDK down 8.2%. original post. @OptionsMike said SMH remains a weak point. UAL was also flagged bearish by multiple accounts for the widespread system outage blocking flights, with @KobeissiLetter and @TrendSpider issuing alerts. original post original post.

Divergence

NVDA is the absolute protagonist with 199 posts, 14 bullish and 25 bearish accounts. @wallstengine highlighted Vera Rubin’s first MLPerf results, leading all 7 AI training benchmarks with per-GPU speed up to 2x faster than GB300. original post. @Mr_Derivatives said going all-in long. But bearish voices are still clearly more numerous. @WheelieInvestor even floated the possibility of GPUs and RAM rising another 10x due to GTA6, with targets of SNDK 10000, MU 2000, NVDA 500, saying no one expected it. original post.

QQQ has 5 vs 9, 33 posts; SPY has 2 vs 8, 38 posts. Indices lean bearish, but individual names like SPCX and some consumer stocks still have support.

Other Noteworthy

Overall, space names gained consensus from the 13F increase, tech outages and chip weakness brought bearish views, and large names like NVDA remain split. 594 posts from 166 accounts, discussion concentrated on these themes.
daily.html:

weekly.brief: Over the past 7 days (Nov 11 to 17) there were 2387 posts from 265 accounts. AMAT remains the clearest consensus bullish with 9 accounts and zero bearish. NU and PANW also have support. NVDA is the biggest hotspot but split, with more bearish (46 vs 27), 955 posts. IWM, MSTR, SMCI are clearer bearish names.
weekly.full:
Consensus

AMAT continued to be favored this week, 9 accounts clearly supportive with zero bearish, 18 posts. Accounts noted sales and profits rising due to semiconductor demand. NU has 4 bullish accounts; @wolfofharcourt showed with a chart that revenue per active customer more than tripled while service costs fell, driving strong operating leverage. PANW also has 4. Overall semiconductor equipment and some consumer tech have consensus.

Joint Bearish

IWM has 5 bearish accounts. MSTR has 4; some called it a macro tragedy, with Saylor’s cost basis around 75500 and Bitcoin below cost. SMCI has 4; posts mentioned the AI trade breaking, NVDA down 36% from highs, etc. Some indices and individual stocks have more consistent negative views.

Divergence

NVDA remains the biggest split, 27 bullish vs 46 bearish, 955 posts. SPCX leans bullish 34 vs 6, 162 posts. QQQ has 8 vs 14, 90 posts. Some see the AI capex story unchanged; others worry about near-term events and valuation.

Other Noteworthy

The weekly data shows equipment names like AMAT with stronger consensus, space names continuing support, but large market and some AI chain under pressure. 2387 posts from 265 accounts.

briefing.html:
Today's Highlights

SPCX has consensus from 10 accounts, with Nvidia’s 13F increasing holdings to 130.5 million shares repeatedly mentioned. NVDA has 199 posts with clearly more bearish accounts than bullish (25 vs 14), despite positive Vera Rubin benchmark results. MSFT was bearish from 5 accounts due to the global outage, and SMH also under pressure from chip weakness.

On a weekly and monthly basis, AMAT and SOFI have stronger consensus, while the broader market and AI leaders continue to diverge.
